The use-case is slightly different. Wavelets are suited for non-stationary signals, while Fourier Transform has no time localization so it's more for stationary signals. Also, a property of wavelets is they're non-parametric, which limits their utility in knowledge discovery applications.

I asked "Which country has the most subway stations?" and got the query

  SELECT ?country (COUNT(*) AS ?stationCount) WHERE {

    ?station wdt:P31 wd:Q928830.
    ?station wdt:P131*/wdt:P17 ?country.
  }
  GROUP BY ?country
  ORDER BY DESC(?stationCount)
  LIMIT 1
https://query.wikidata.org/#SELECT%20%3Fcountry%20%28COUNT%2...

In this case it doesn't change the answer (it only finds 3 more subway stations in China), but sometimes it does.

I recently asked some of the SOTA models to generate a webGL application for the Hopf fibration.
